title: Nobody Finishes Last, Explained
subtitle: Eskil Nwabueze on what community sport clubs do about the last line of their results
summary: A research explainer from the School of Continuous Improvement on Eskil Nwabueze's doctoral thesis about the bottom row of a club's results sheet. It follows the appointed last, the volunteer rostered to finish behind everyone, from a census of club series through the weekly timed runs and a trial in eighteen series, and closes on the School's own Last Place Roster. Nwabueze describes the work in his own words.
topic: A research explainer of the doctoral thesis on what community sport clubs do about last place on their results sheets, following the appointed last through a census of club series, an archive of weekly timed runs with and without a tail walker, an interview study and a stepped-wedge trial, to the School's Last Place Roster

beats.text: A ranked list always has a bottom row. It can be reassigned, but not removed.
Under the School’s new Last Place Roster, every ranked list it publishes will carry a member of staff, one place below the last genuine entrant, with nothing written beside it.
